blocks.html: This chapter puts the testing framework of Chapter 8 to work on the commonest research question: do these groups differ? It starts with z-tests for a mean and for proportions (§9.1), moves to the t-test family for means (§9.2), checks the Normality assumption these tests lean on and what to do when it fails (§9.3–§9.4), and ends with ANOVA for three or more groups, including how to handle many comparisons at once (§9.5). Every test here is “parametric”: it assumes the data, or the sampling distribution of the statistic, is approximately Normal. Chapter 10 gives the alternatives when that assumption is not defensible.
